final_acceptance.reason: The visible stem’s two requested parts are covered by all four complete options; D is factually supported by the reviewed theory and CTFL context. The wrong models are defensible, complete misconceptions. Form, section relevance, linkage, ANSC, and Russian readability were reviewed. Original Q1 FACTS was UNVERIFIED at that point; the source addendum verified the cited CTFL context and upgraded FACTS to PASS. The exact standalone strategy wording is contextual, not a normative CTFL definition.

B matches the supplied theory and the checked primary sources: Cohn’s unit/service/UI model and CTFL’s granularity/allocation description. All options address both what the pyramid is and its application; the wrong answers are complete, rebuttable models. Form, section relevance, linkage, ANSC, professional tone, and readability were reviewed. The exact risk/feedback-cost allocation clause is contextual guidance, not a formal rule stated by those sources.

A aligns with Principles of Chaos Engineering on hypothesis, measurable steady state, controlled perturbation, comparison, and minimizing blast radius. All three wrong answers were examined, including the value of exploratory observations and local stub tests; their overclaims remain false. All seven review axes were assessed, with relevant sections and comparable professional option form.

A is supported by the reviewed theory and Fowler’s distinction between stub responses and mock interaction verification. Counterexamples show that a stubbed repository need not execute SQL and that correct call order does not entail a correct computed result. All wrong answers are complete, defensible misconceptions; completeness, section linkage, form, tone, and Russian readability were reviewed. Runtime API behavior was not executed and is outside this conceptual acceptance.

sources.used_for: Definition as controlled system experiment; measurable steady state; hypothesis in control and experiment groups; introduce real-world variables; compare outcomes to try to disprove hypothesis; minimize and contain blast radius.
sources.version: Principles of Chaos Engineering, page states last update March 2019

sources.used_for: Mock objects are one form of test double; Fowler distinguishes state verification from behavior verification, and stubs from mocks. This supports separating configured responses from interaction expectations. The local-review counterexample is that a stubbed repository can return canned data without executing SQL; proper real-database verification therefore requires an appropriate real dependency.
sources.version: Article dated 02 January 2007; no separate revision version stated

sources.used_for: Mike Cohn describes unit as the largest/base layer, UI at the top and minimized, and service testing as the middle layer covering application services separately from UI. Supports B’s broad ordering/distribution; it does not establish that all tests must run in that sequence.

§5.1.1: test plan describes objectives, resources, processes and means/schedule, helps meet criteria, and demonstrates adherence to test policy/strategy or explains deviations. §5.1.6: pyramid models differing test granularity and supports automation/effort allocation; layer number/names may differ and high-level tests are generally slower and cover broader functionality. It does not define a standalone strategy document or equate strategy with metric lists/reports.
